summary: The live web integrator treats agent-nix capacity refusals as retryable tick errors instead of broken candidate builds. Refused candidates and attribution probes retain the served build without poisoning the failed-tree cache or ejecting a PR.

compatibility.detail: Integrator tick JSONL now reports build=error, reason=capacity-refused and retryable=true for EX_TEMPFAIL (75). Observers should distinguish this host-capacity outcome from candidate build failures. A capacity refusal during the reduced-candidate rebuild after attribution withholds the failure-cache write and restores the tentative included/skipped PR lists. Wire contracts and INTEGRATOR_VERSION are unchanged.

downtime.detail: The served build remains active during a capacity refusal; the next tick retries the candidate.

manual.detail: No new configuration. Existing failed-tree entries written by older integrators are not automatically reclassified; an operator must remove a confirmed capacity-poisoned entry before it can retry.

recovery.detail: Allow host capacity to recover and let the next tick retry. Rolling back restores the previous exit-code handling and can again cache capacity refusals as build failures; no storage rollback or migration is required.
